name: Handle liens and adjudication
summary: Trades that are unpaid can register a lien against the project, which makes owners and lenders hold back payment to the contractor, and since October 2019 Ontario trades and contractors can also send payment disputes to a fast statutory adjudication. Contracts counsel checks each lien against the trade's payment record and the project manager's account of the dispute, tries to settle, and otherwise posts a surety bond and gets a court order vacating the lien so the owner keeps paying. The same group answers or starts adjudications and the notices that follow an owner's refusal to pay. Short statutory deadlines, records split between the ERP and the project team, and waits on the surety and the court drive the work.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with a small in-house legal group supporting about 220 active building projects, with most volume in Ontario.
baseline.notes: Ontario's Construction Act prompt payment and adjudication rules took effect on 1 October 2019; Western and Atlantic provinces had lien statutes but no adjudication in most of the period.

trigger: A trade registers or preserves a lien on a project, a trade serves a notice of adjudication, or an owner serves a notice of non-payment on a progress invoice.
end_state: The lien is discharged, lapses or becomes a lien action; the adjudication determination is paid; or the owner dispute is settled.

volume.seasonality: More liens at the end of projects and during the winter slowdown when trades press for payment.

evidence.note: Author's estimate, below the organisation file's 4-8-14. Ontario-wide only 50 (fiscal 2021) and 121 (fiscal 2022) adjudications were started, of which about 16 and 39 were commercial, public buildings or industrial (src osler_odacc2, osler_odacc3), so this contractor is party to only a few a year; lien volume is set at about one a month per 40 to 50 active projects.
Runs every matter; FTE is the author's estimate. Loaded cost from the organisation file (salaried wage x 1.35).

systems.name: Government portals (WSIB clearance, Ministry of Labour notice of project, CRA, land registry)
Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)

steps.name: Log the lien, adjudication or non-payment notice
steps.description: Contracts counsel receives the document, usually forwarded by the owner, the project manager or the land registry search: a claim for lien registered by a trade, a trade's notice of adjudication, or an owner's notice of non-payment. They open a matter, record the project, claimant, amount and service date.
inputs: claim for lien, notice of adjudication or owner notice of non-payment

evidence.note: Lien and adjudication notices under the Ontario Construction Act; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Classify the matter and diarise deadlines
steps.description: Contracts counsel decides which path applies and diarises the statutory deadlines: lien perfection and expiry, adjudication response dates, and the 7-day and 21-day steps that follow an owner's notice of non-payment.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario): lien preservation within 60 days and perfection within 90 days after the last preservation date

next.condition: lien registered or preserved by a trade
trade served a notice of adjudication
owner served a notice of non-payment

evidence.note: Deadlines from the law firm summaries; path shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the claimant's payment status
steps.description: The project accountant pulls the claimant's subcontract ledger from the ERP: contract value, approved changes, invoices, payments, holdback retained and amounts held back for disputes or back-charges.

error.defect_description: Unapproved change or back-charge left out.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Explain the underlying dispute
steps.description: The project manager writes up why the trade is unpaid: disputed extras, deficiencies, back-charges, a default or a payment the owner has not made. They attach correspondence and the subcontract change log.

evidence.note: Payment disputes most often concern valuation of work and payment under the contract, including change orders; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess the lien's validity and exposure
steps.description: Contracts counsel checks whether the lien was preserved in time, names the right owner and property, and is not inflated beyond the unpaid contract price, and estimates the company's exposure including costs.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario): lien preservation within 60 days and perfection within 90 days after the last preservation date

evidence.note: 60-day preservation period; defective share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Demand discharge of a defective lien
steps.description: Contracts counsel writes to the claimant or its lawyer setting out why the lien is out of time or improper and demanding a discharge, warning that the company will seek costs on a motion.

error.defect_description: Demand sent to the wrong party.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Negotiate payment with the claimant
steps.description: The project manager meets or calls the trade to agree what is owed after back-charges and deficiencies, and offers to release undisputed amounts in exchange for a discharge.

error.defect_description: Settlement does not cover sub-sub claims.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Request a lien bond from the surety
steps.description: The treasury, surety and credit manager asks the surety for a lien bond for the lien amount plus the statutory costs allowance, or arranges a letter of credit, and sends the surety the lien and indemnity documents.

error.defect_description: Bond amount below the required security.

evidence.note: Security may be cash, an irrevocable letter of credit or a lien bond.

steps.name: Wait for the surety's lien bond
steps.description: The surety underwrites and issues the bond under the company's bonding facility. Cash security is used instead when the owner needs the lien off title within days.

evidence.note: Cash is used when urgent, bonds when there is less urgency; duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Bring a motion to vacate the lien
steps.description: Contracts counsel, usually with external counsel, prepares the motion record with an affidavit, the bond and a draft order, and files it with the Superior Court. The security must equal the lien amount plus 25%, capped at $250,000, for costs.

error.defect_description: Security short of the statutory amount.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario) s.44: security of the lien amount plus 25% (up to $250,000) for costs to vacate a lien

evidence.note: Section 44 security amount and court order from the law firm summary.

steps.name: Wait for the court order and registration
steps.description: The court issues the order to vacate once the security reaches the Accountant of the Superior Court, and the order is registered on title. The owner can then release funds it held because of the lien.

evidence.note: Order follows delivery of security to the Accountant; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Ask the owner to release held funds
steps.description: Contracts counsel sends the owner the registered vacating order and asks it to release the amount it withheld from the company's progress payments because of the lien.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Watch the perfection deadline and keep negotiating
steps.description: Contracts counsel tracks whether the claimant starts an action to perfect the lien within 90 days, while the project manager keeps negotiating. An unperfected lien expires and the security is returned.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario): lien preservation within 60 days and perfection within 90 days after the last preservation date

evidence.note: 90-day perfection period; outcome shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the settlement payment
steps.description: The regional finance manager approves the settlement payment against the subcontract ledger, checking it does not pay twice for amounts already paid or held as holdback.

control.basis: Payments outside the regular subcontract invoice run approved by finance, separate from the negotiating project manager

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Pay the claimant against a discharge
steps.description: The project accountant issues the settlement cheque or transfer in exchange for a signed discharge of the lien, held in escrow by counsel until the funds clear.

error.defect_description: Payment coded to the wrong subcontract.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm the discharge is registered
steps.description: Contracts counsel checks the land registry or the owner's records to confirm the discharge is registered or delivered, then asks for any posted security to be returned and closes the matter.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess the trade's notice of adjudication
steps.description: Contracts counsel reads the trade's notice of adjudication, checks that the dispute is one that can be adjudicated and that the contract dates qualify, and decides whether to consent to the named adjudicator.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario) Part II.1 adjudication: adjudicator appointment, documents within 5 days, determination within 30 days

evidence.note: 24 of 121 adjudications started in fiscal 2022 were terminated, some because the contract pre-dated October 2019.

steps.name: Wait for the adjudicator and the claimant's documents
steps.description: The named adjudicator consents, or ODACC appoints one, and the claimant delivers its documents. The 30-day clock for the determination starts when the adjudicator receives them.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario) Part II.1 adjudication: adjudicator appointment, documents within 5 days, determination within 30 days

evidence.note: Consent within 4 days, ODACC appointment within 7 days, documents within 5 days of appointment.

steps.name: Gather project evidence for the adjudication
steps.description: The project manager assembles the subcontract, change records, daily reports, photos and correspondence that answer the claim and writes a statement of the facts for counsel.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the adjudication submission
steps.description: Contracts counsel writes the submission for the company, whether responding to a trade or claiming against an owner, with the evidence package and a calculation of the amount, and delivers it to the adjudicator and the other party.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario) Part II.1 adjudication: adjudicator appointment, documents within 5 days, determination within 30 days

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the determination
steps.description: The adjudicator reviews the documents, may ask questions or hold a short call, and issues a written determination. About three-quarters are issued within 30 days; the rest are extended by consent.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario) Part II.1 adjudication: adjudicator appointment, documents within 5 days, determination within 30 days

evidence.note: 79% (fiscal 2021) and 75% (fiscal 2022) of determinations within the 30-day timeline.

steps.name: Pay or collect the determined amount
steps.description: The project accountant pays the determined amount to the trade, or records and collects the amount the owner was ordered to pay, within 10 days of the determination, and the matter is closed or referred to court if a party seeks review.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario): payment within 10 days of an adjudicator's determination

evidence.note: Payment within 10 days of the determination.

steps.name: Notify trades of the owner's non-payment
steps.description: When the owner disputes part of a proper invoice, contracts counsel issues the company's notice of non-payment to the affected trades with a copy of the owner's notice and an undertaking to refer the dispute to adjudication within 21 days.
outputs: contractor notice of non-payment and undertaking

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario) prompt payment: contractor notice of non-payment within 7 days of the owner's notice, with an undertaking to adjudicate within 21 days

evidence.note: Prompt payment deadlines from the law firm summary.

steps.name: Negotiate the disputed amount with the owner
steps.description: The project manager meets the owner and consultant to resolve the disputed portion of the invoice before the adjudication referral deadline. Disputes not settled go to adjudication against the owner.

evidence.note: 21-day undertaking to adjudicate; settlement share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Serve a notice of adjudication on the owner
steps.description: Contracts counsel drafts and serves the notice of adjudication on the owner naming a proposed adjudicator from the ODACC registry, and registers the adjudication with ODACC.

control.basis: Construction Act (Ontario) Part II.1 adjudication: adjudicator appointment, documents within 5 days, determination within 30 days

evidence.note: Adjudication starts with a notice naming a proposed adjudicator.

exceptions.name: Lien vacated by posting security
exceptions.description: No settlement is reached quickly, so the company posts a surety bond and obtains a court order removing the lien from title.

exceptions.name: Defective lien
exceptions.description: The lien was preserved late or is otherwise improper and counsel demands a discharge.

exceptions.name: Adjudication
exceptions.description: A trade starts an adjudication against the company, or the company starts one against an owner after a notice of non-payment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt of the lien or notice to closure or hand-off
benchmarks.population: Liens and adjudications on a Canadian general contractor's building projects, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the statutory clock: about 40 to 50 days for an adjudication (appointment, 5 days for documents, 30 days to decide, 10 to pay), about 4 to 8 weeks to vacate a lien, and up to 90 days more for perfection.

benchmarks.population: All ODACC adjudications in Ontario, all sectors

pain_points.description: Each lien makes the owner hold back payment to the company until it is vacated or settled.

evidence.note: Owners seek to remove liens urgently; even a few days' delay may be material.

pain_points.description: Counsel depends on the ERP and the project manager to learn what is actually owed, which takes days.

evidence.note: Author's observation of common practice.

pain_points.description: Statutory deadlines leave little time to assemble an adjudication response.

evidence.note: Documents within 5 days of appointment and a decision within 30 days.

sources.title: Prompt payment and adjudication have arrived in Ontario
sources.supports: Adjudication starts with a notice of adjudication naming a proposed adjudicator; if the adjudicator does not consent within 4 days ODACC appoints one within 7 days; claimant documents within 5 days of appointment; determination within 30 days of receiving documents, extendable only by consent; payment within 10 days of the determination or work may be suspended; lien preservation 60 days (was 45) and perfection 90 days after the last preservation date.

sources.title: Prompt Payment for Construction in Ontario
sources.supports: Owner pays a proper invoice within 28 days; owner notice of non-payment within 14 days; contractor pays subcontractors within 7 days of payment; contractor notice of non-payment within 7 days of the owner's notice or 35 days after the invoice, with a copy of the owner's notice and an undertaking to refer the matter to adjudication within 21 days.

sources.title: The fine print: form and sufficiency of letters of credit to vacate liens
sources.supports: Under Construction Act s.44 a party may vacate a lien by posting security with the Superior Court equal to the full lien amount plus 25% of it (up to $250,000) for costs; security may be cash, an irrevocable letter of credit or a lien bond; cash is used when urgent, bonds or letters of credit otherwise; the court issues an order to vacate once the approved security reaches the Accountant of the Superior Court.

sources.title: Adjudication: ODACC releases second annual report
sources.supports: ODACC fiscal 2021 (to 31 July 2021): 50 adjudications commenced (32 in fiscal 2020); 34 determinations (3 in fiscal 2020); 79% within the 30-day timeline, the rest extended; about $8.7 million claimed, average $174,193; $908,123 awarded, average $26,710; disputes mainly valuation of services and payment under a contract including change orders; none on holdback; commercial 10, public buildings 3, industrial 3 of 50.

sources.title: Adjudication: ODACC releases third annual report
sources.supports: ODACC fiscal 2022 (1 August 2021 to 31 July 2022): 121 adjudications commenced; 24 terminated; 67 determinations, 75% within 30 days; about $33.5 million claimed, average $277,168; $3,449,619 awarded; mostly valuation and payment disputes including change orders; residential 52, transportation and infrastructure 30, commercial 23, public buildings 10, industrial 6.

assumptions: Ontario rules are used for all matters; most volume is in the Ontario region and other provinces' lien statutes follow similar preservation, vacating and perfection steps.
Ontario statutes could not be opened directly; rules are taken from law firm summaries and treated as tier B.
Liens on public land are preserved by notice to the owner rather than registered on title, but follow the same vacating and settlement steps.
Lien actions after perfection are handed to the claims and litigation process.
External counsel and the surety are outside parties; their time is modelled as waits.
Waits include nights and weekends; legal and finance roles work weekdays.
